name: Shelah
overview: Shelah is a male biblical figure identified primarily as the son of Arpachshad. Scripture records little else about him beyond this direct genealogical connection. No tribe or additional notes are specified for Shelah, indicating his role as a link in the ancestral lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Shelah means 'to send' and is a proper name mentioned in Genesis 10:24. The name was not given by God but carries a meaning that may reflect a purposeful sending or continuation within the biblical genealogy.
familyAndRelationships: Shelah is explicitly identified as the father of Eber and is inferred to be the son of Arpachshad. These relationships place him within the early post-Flood genealogical line, connecting key patriarchal figures in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Shelah's significance lies in his position within the genealogical record following the Flood, serving as a crucial link in the ancestry that leads to Eber, an important patriarch. This lineage is foundational for understanding the development of the peoples descended from Shelah's family. His mention underscores God's providential preservation and unfolding plan through successive generations.
